titolo: Adjustment and growth in the euro area
frase: For the remainder of my remarks, I would like to first review the ongoing process of adjustment across the euro area and what has been done by national authorities, and the ECB acting within its price stability mandate, to facilitate that process.

titolo: Adjustment and growth in the euro area
frase: While the ECB has consistently played its part and maintained price stability in the euro area, it is important to keep in mind that the role that the central bank can play in terms of crisis resolution is limited.

titolo: Adjustment and growth in the euro area
frase: The ECB’s monetary policy can only play a crisis mitigation role.

titolo: Adjustment and growth in the euro area
frase: Hence, our monetary policy approach has focused on providing liquidity support, intended to relieve banks of liquidity and funding stress by giving them unlimited access to central bank money at a fixed price against adequate collateral.

titolo: Adjustment and growth in the euro area
frase: This was necessary in order to avoid deflationary downward pressures that would have prevented us from delivering on our mandate of preserving price stability in the euro area.

titolo: Adjustment and growth in the euro area
frase: However, to mitigate the crisis we have also had to go beyond liquidity support, in particular to counter financial fragmentation in the euro area – created by the adverse feedback loops I described above – that was disrupting the transmission of monetary policy across the euro area.

titolo: Adjustment and growth in the euro area
frase: Diverging credit conditions by countries, by sectors and by size of companies have prevented the ECB’s very accommodative monetary policy stance from being passed on evenly in the financing conditions faced by euro area firms and households.

titolo: Adjustment and growth in the euro area
frase: As the euro area economy relies heavily on bank credit, this has serious implications for growth and ultimately for our ability to maintain price stability.

titolo: Adjustment and growth in the euro area
frase: We therefore decided to open the possibility of undertaking Outright Monetary Transactions (OMTs), entailing ex ante unlimited interventions in short- to medium-term securities issued by governments which have submitted to strict and effective conditionality, in order to eliminate the pricing of un-warranted tail risks in the bond markets.

titolo: Adjustment and growth in the euro area
frase: This has played an important role in reducing financial market fragmentation, as financial markets understood OMTs as a credible backstop for countering redenomination risk.

titolo: Adjustment and growth in the euro area
frase: In this context, it is necessary to review consolidation strategies that have relied predominantly on tax rate increases, exacerbating the burden on already compliant taxpayers, without much broadening of the tax bases.

titolo: Adjustment and growth in the euro area
frase: For its part, the ECB will continue to fulfil its mandate to maintain price stability, and to use its standard and non-standard measures to support the flow of credit to the real economy.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: I would like to use this opportunity to reflect on a fundamental tension lying at the heart of monetary policy:

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: A central bank’s success in ensuring macroeconomic stability depends on it having a credible commitment to price stability.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: This, in turn, challenges monetary policy-makers to temporarily adapt their established strategies to a new environment without undermining their inflation-fighting credentials.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: As a consequence, the link between monetary policy impulses and economic aggregates – which is the structural relationship most relevant for central banks – was severely affected.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: But they have also triggered a lively debate on where to draw the line between crisis-fighting efforts on the one hand – and a general departure from established principles of monetary policy on the other.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: I will argue that the key to success lies in a clear-cut hierarchy between the different elements of a monetary policy strategy.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: The monetary policy objective of a central bank should always be the overriding concern and guiding principle of any policy action.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: As I will demonstrate, the ECB’s monetary policy strategy during the crisis has consistently taken this approach.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: Elements of a monetary policy strategy Let me first briefly expand on the distinction between the different elements of a monetary policy strategy.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: What I refer to as monetary policy objectives are the overarching economic goals of a central bank.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: For most central banks around the globe, these goals include – as a primary component – the pursuit of price stability.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: In the modern central banking universe that has emerged since the macroeconomic failures of the 1970s, no one would doubt that while price stability is a desirable medium-term goal for monetary policy.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: These objectives are ancillary because they have more to do with the path to the medium-term objective – a path that should minimise unnecessary fluctuations under way – than with the medium-term objective itself, which remains price stability.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: By contrast, the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union clearly specifies price stability as the primary objective for the Eurosystem.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: The conduct of monetary policy refers to the way a central bank goes about achieving its objective.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: The aggregates are chosen because of their close empirical association with the variables underlying the ultimate monetary policy objectives.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: They may include, for example, broad monetary aggregates or market interest rates.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: These include reserve requirements, the monetary base, as well as the key interest rates at which the central bank provides liquidity to market participants.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: Changes in monetary policy strategy have very different implications, depending on which of these two constituent elements – policy objectives or policy conduct – they affect.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: In the euro area, for example, the price stability objective has “constitutional” status: it is explicitly laid down in Article 127(1) of the Treaty.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: At the same time, the institutional framework leaves considerable scope for the Eurosystem to calibrate its policy measures so that it achieves its price stability objective.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: Interactions between the conduct of monetary policy and its objectives The success of a monetary policy strategy depends on the interaction between these elements: the more credible a central bank’s commitment to its objective, the more flexibly it can adjust its monetary policy conduct to specific challenges.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: And this can change the way society perceives the basic parameters of the monetary policy framework.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: Inflation expectations – one prominent parameter of how the regime is perceived by the public – can become unanchored.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: Second, a credible commitment to the objective allows a central bank to tailor the strength and timing of its monetary policy response more specifically to the shocks that hit the economy from time to time.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: In the case of a negative demand shock, both economic activity and inflation will tend to fall.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: Typically, a financial crisis is one example of a negative demand shock: credit conditions are restricted, aggregate demand is restrained and firms are encouraged to undercut their competitors, thereby exerting downward pressure on inflation.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: To the extent warranted by the magnitude of the shock, the central bank thus faces an unambiguous policy prescription, namely to provide additional monetary accommodation.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: In the case of a negative supply shock, the central bank has a policy dilemma as economic activity and inflation move in opposite directions.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: Here, the central bank either temporarily accepts higher inflation, or – in an attempt to keep inflation right on target – it reinforces the disturbance driving down output.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: But this trade-off is weakened when the central bank can credibly commit to its price stability objective.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: Knowing that the steady state remains the ultimate goal of policy, private agents will not factor in the temporary increase in inflation into their price- and wage-setting behaviour.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: The flexibility of policy conduct is clearly limited to those measures that preserve the central bank’s room for manoeuvre to independently determine its monetary policy stance – now and in the future.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: The monetary policy strategy of the ECB Let me relate this analysis to the monetary policy strategy of the ECB.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: As I mentioned earlier, the Treaty unambiguously establishes price stability as the primary objective of the ECB.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: On this basis, the Governing Council has communicated an explicit definition of price stability, namely a range of positive inflation rates below 2% over the medium term.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: This is a range at which inflation does not distort the allocation of resources in the economy.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: This clear objective, together with the ECB’s track record, has firmly anchored inflation expectations in the euro area.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: Since 1999, the average inflation expectation by professional forecasters at a five year horizon has been on average 1.91%.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: In our framework, inflation is obviously an indicator of pre-eminent policy relevance.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: In conducting its policy, the ECB has looked at a broader set of indicators which from time to time have released signals which conflicted with those which we extracted from our inflation forecast.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: Since the 1990s and for much of the last decade, inflation in a large number of mature industrial economies remained quiescent.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: A regained control of inflation expectations by the major monetary authorities was certainly a prime cause of price stability.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: But other factors contributed to a sustained trend of disinflation.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: In the euro area, despite the upward pressures that the ongoing adjustment in relative price levels across Member States was exerting on the euro area price index, “price pressures”- defined as the difference between the year-on-year harmonised inflation rate observed in each quarter and the upper ceiling of our price stability range of 2% - were absent or even negative in the years preceding the Lehman debacle.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: Had the ECB relied on inflation as a summary statistic of the state of the economy, the conclusion would have been that the economy had reached an ideal state of balanced, non-inflationary growth – the “Great Moderation”.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: The price stability objective needs to be reinforced, in the day-to-day conduct of policy, by an intense strategic focus on monetary and financial indicators.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: When financial markets create excessive leverage – too much credit – and engage in imprudent maturity transformation – too much bank money – reacting to financial booms under the monetary pillar will not only ensure price stability but also counteract the build-up of risk.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: Vice versa, very subdued credit dynamics, such as those we are currently observing, provide crucial signals of how long the accommodative monetary stance is warranted.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: But the possibility of activating this fail-safe policy mechanism largely depends on how the price stability objective is defined.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: The fact that inflation can move within a certain range is an important pre-condition.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: First, there is some flexibility as to where inflation could be within the range at any point in time.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: In 2003 the Governing Council announced that within the range of inflation rates consistent with price stability, a rate “close to 2%” should be the aim of policy in the medium term.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: But there is scope for inflation to vary within the range along the way to convergence with the medium-term policy aim, and many path configurations are possible.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: Second, the medium term itself is not a pre-set time span, but it is dependent on the underlying shocks that may explain inflation dynamics from time to time.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: The former type of discretion – related to the path of convergence of inflation to its medium-term level – is critical when supply shocks are positive, that is, expansionary and disinflationary.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: This dimension of the ECB’s monetary policy strategy is not always appreciated, but is important.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: When inflation pressures are absent or negative and positive shocks to aggregate supply feed financial buoyancy – the conditions which prevailed in the late 1990s and for a good part of the 2000s – having a range definition of price stability, rather than, say, a point target, is essential.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: The possibility of letting inflation temporarily drift down within its price stability range when faced with clear signs of financial exuberance increases the chances of hitting the inflation objective over the long run.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: For example, a cost-push shock deriving from a spike in commodity prices pushes measured inflation upwards and is a drain on demand and economic activity.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: A negative demand shock which is recessionary and potentially deflationary will have to be counteracted quickly and forcefully.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: This is what we have to do if confronted with severe downside risks to price stability.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: Against this background, let me briefly come back to the comparison between the ECB’s monetary policy framework and that of the Federal Reserve System in the US.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: As mentioned earlier, the mandates of these two central banks differ: the ECB’s framework entails a clear ordering of objectives in which price stability ranks first, whereas the Fed’s dual mandate focuses on both price stability and maximum employment.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: To see this, we should bear in mind that monetary policy can only support real economic aggregates in the short run.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: Any attempt by monetary policy to permanently lift the economy above the growth potential determined by these factors is bound to fail.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: But, as I just explained, the ECB’s price stability definition and policy horizon also allow for substantial flexibility in calibrating the policy response to shocks.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: Due to this flexibility, the ECB can pursue its long-term price stability objective without triggering socially costly short-run fluctuations in output and employment.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: However, funding conditions for firms and households constitute a key channel through which monetary policy impulses translate into consumption and investment decisions.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: In a similar vein, the programme for Outright Monetary Transactions has been designed with a view to combatting fragmentation while preserving the credibility of the ECB’s monetary policy objective.

titolo: Monetary policy in the crisis - Confronting short-run challenges while anchoring long-run expectations
frase: And sovereign solvency is a necessary condition to avoid fiscal dominance on monetary policy, and thereby for the ECB to fulfil its medium term objective.

frase: A third example is the ECB’s action to improve the transmission to the real economy of the impulsions provided by the single monetary policy.

titolo: Outright Monetary Transactions, one year on

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: A key factor for a full recovery of the euro area economy and ensuring that inflation does not remain too low for too long will be the extra stimulus that the Governing Council decided to introduce in January under the ECB’s expanded asset purchase program.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: First, the momentum supporting the economic recovery was viewed as too weak and fragile to give us sufficient confidence that inflation would return to levels closer to 2% over a policy relevant medium-term horizon.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Second, the expansive potential of the monetary policy measures that had been decided between June and October was seen as uncertain.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Therefore, the monetary impulse had to be reinforced and needed to be quantitatively more predictable and controllable to put the economy and the outlook for price stability on a firmer footing.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: On 9 March, we started purchasing public-sector securities as part of our expanded asset purchase programme, which also comprises interventions in the ABS and covered bond markets.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Overall, our asset purchases will amount to €60 billion per month.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: What is new today, however, is that lower interest rates in capital markets are increasingly being transmitted through the entire financial intermediation chain.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: We intend to carry out our purchases at least until end-September 2016, and in any case until we see a sustained adjustment in the path of inflation which is consistent with our aim of achieving inflation rates below, but close to, 2% over the medium term.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: The Governing Council will take a holistic perspective when assessing the path of inflation.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: It will evaluate the likelihood for inflation not only to converge to levels that are closer to 2%, but also to stabilize around those levels with sufficient confidence thereafter.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
parole_chiave: governing council; inflation; monetary policy; price stability
frase: When doing this assessment, the Governing Council will follow its monetary policy strategy and concentrate on inflation trends, looking through any surprise in measured inflation (in either direction) if judged to be transient and with no implications for the medium term outlook for price stability.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: The combination of improved economic structures and sound fiscal policies indeed has the potential to make our monetary policy more effective by encouraging economic actors to take advantage of improved financing conditions and increase investment.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Price stability and financial stability Let me now turn, as suggested by the ECON coordinators, to the interaction between price stability and financial stability.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Price stability is, as you know, the primary objective of the ECB and the Eurosystem.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: And achieving price stability is a necessary condition for financial stability.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Clearly, unstable inflation developments can distort a wide variety of macroeconomic and financial fluctuations, to the extent that these distortions become harmful for the economy.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: For example, unstable inflation developments could complicate pricing of assets and blur the signals from relative asset price adjustments with detrimental effects on resource allocation.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: However, price stability is not a sufficient condition of financial stability.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: The last crisis proved that financial stability can be at risk even at times when price stability is achieved.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: And monetary policy decisions also affect expectations and a wide range of asset prices.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Our monetary policy measures are necessary to achieve our primary objective of maintaining price stability.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: At the same time, financial stability is a precondition for the efficient conduct of monetary policy.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
parole_chiave: monetary policy; price stability; transmission mechanism
frase: To be successful in delivering price stability, monetary policy relies on the effectiveness of the monetary transmission mechanism.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: In this context, a stable and non-fragmented financial system is important for the smooth transmission of monetary policy signals.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Gualtieri: Thank you, President Draghi for your intervention, and also for having addressed the point we asked on price stability and financial stability, indeed underlining the importance of the role of macro-prudential instruments in this regard.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: And then thirdly, very briefly, could I just say what about the low levels of inflation and combating that in the Eurozone.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Is it sticking by its policy of low inflation rates given that so many things have been reduced to the point where borrowers may be unsettled by that?

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Your other question is about the inflation rate and price stability.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: We believe that the recovery in inflation in our projections, - as I mentioned, it is going to be zero this year, 1.5% next year, 1.7% the year thereafter - is conditional on the full implementation of our expanded asset purchase programme.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: As inflation is predicated to go back to the level close but below 2%, and as recovery will firm up, so will interest rates naturally follow.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: We are certainly aware of the situation that savers in the euro area have to bear with because of the low interest rates and we are certainly, as I have just said in the introductory statement, we certainly are aware of the potential financial stability risks that a protracted situation of low interest rates might entail.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: And that may be particularly true in areas where your mandate isn’t so clear as it is when it comes to inflation.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Now, your second question is about the structural reforms, is about which additional policies are needed to give full effectiveness to our monetary policy and there, as I said in the initial statement and I never would say made a mystery of, I think that our monetary policy can actually be fully complemented by the member states undertaking structural reforms and each member state has its own agenda.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Here I beg to differ with those who say QE has reduced the incentive of member states to undertake structural reforms because it keeps the interest rate so low that member states will have no interest, or no incentive to do so.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Lower interest rates make investment projects that were previously unattractive attractive and this is the key benefit, of course.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: That’s why the structural reforms become an important component of the final positive outcomes that our monetary policy will produce.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Now, of course, with responsibility for monetary policy in the Eurozone your main job is maintaining price stability and you are independent.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Is that monetary policy or is that a policy instrument which should be debated with the parliament and decided with the parliament?

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: The second question, you’re actually asking whether QE is a monetary policy instrument or not.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: We obviously are convinced it is a monetary policy instrument.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: This issue has been, I would say, marginally dealt with also in the opinion of the lawyer - I think it’s called the General Lawyer - of the European Court of Justice and it was found compliant regarding OMT, - admittedly not QE -, and it is found compliant with Article 123.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: So, we continue basically to assess the purchases of sovereign debt on the secondary market as being a tool of monetary policy.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Now, you’ve been blackmailing, I think, and are you aware of how this type of blackmail that has been led by the ECB has endangered monetary policy?

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: I mean, I know that this of course is rather fragmented, of course, but the ECB’s monetary policy really is helping some and suffocating others and that’s what is happening to Greece and thank you for being so clear.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Can I focus on quantitative easing, in particular the new estimates for growth in the outlook for the Eurozone done by the ECB?

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: It seems to me that these estimates, these forecasts, on the effects of monetary policy at the ECB are a little bit self-referential.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: They are positive, but it does assume the beneficial effects of quantitative easing, of QE.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: But the Central Bank is also saying that QE and other instruments will have an impact on future developments with regard to the expectations regarding inflation in the Eurozone.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Then secondly, with inflation estimates, at a recent press conference and recent speeches you have been expressing optimism about the future inflation expectations.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: For example, the five-year expectation for the inflation rate which has demonstrated not to be itself, not to be entirely opportune when it comes to getting that estimate of future inflation rates right.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Should you not use other indicators which are more consistent with the time frame in terms of producing monetary policy effects?

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: And, also, have a track record when it comes to the five-year outlook, perhaps two years/two years forward inflation rate which currently demonstrates how inflation expectations are not entirely in line with the statutory duties of the ECB.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: It basically says that an expansionary monetary policy will raise inflation expectations in the medium-term.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: When inflation expectations go up with zero nominal rates, real rates go down.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: At some point in time inflation expectations did worsen so that real rates actually have gone up and this was equivalent to an unwanted tightening of monetary policy.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: The decrease in inflation expectations, the medium-term inflation expectations that took place between November and December was equivalent in terms of tightening to the last decreases in nominal rates that we had undertaken.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: In other words, it nullified our more expansionary monetary policy decisions when we decided to lower nominal rates before.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: With QE, we see now that inflation expectations… You pick up an indicator, whatever you want, but it has to be medium-term, inflation expectations have actually improved.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: It can go backward and back up again because we had low inflation for such a long time that there is an inborn inertia in these indicators and, in fact, all our projections are medium-term projections.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: So, as I said, we need a sustained, I think I used the word sustained, adjustment in the inflation path.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: We will not be taking decisions for temporary blips in inflation rates and we will not take decisions based on figures at each point in time and our projections are conditional on the full implementation of this programme.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: I should say also that there are good reasons for forecasting that inflation expectations will move back towards 2% but below 2%.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: As I said, one is, of course, our monetary policy decision.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Having used all your cartridges, monetary policy is really non-conventional with TLTROs and I bring up member state debt.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: That’s a last chance salon thing and it doesn’t respect the Tinbergen principles set out in the provisions of the Treaty, not using monetary policy for purposes other than price stability, 127(a), not financing states via the Eurosystem and not using monetary policy for exchange policy purposes 219.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Draghi: Well, first of all, let me say that our monetary policy is gradually finding its way to the real economy.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: So, it’s not only limited in its impact to the financial markets, as it actually was in 2012 after the August decision of OMT.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: My view is that we pursue the price stability rule and mandate and we stick with our mandate and we have no fiscal policy in mind.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: So, our monetary policy will stay accommodative for the foreseeable future and other jurisdictions’ monetary policies are expected to become tighter and tighter because the recovery is stronger in these jurisdictions than it is in our case.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: President, when you launched the QE quantitative easing programme we were all aware that this was in the spirit of doing all within your power to ensure that the Eurozone could continue to function.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: On the first question, our QE, if successful, will raise medium-term inflation expectations and, therefore, lower real interest rates and, therefore, contribute to price stability and the recovery of the euro area.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: In the monetary policy area, before the euro, we were, in a sense, a rule-based monetary policy system.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: But so far, certainly the experience in the fiscal area has not been as successful as been the experience in the monetary policy area.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: The ECB monetary policy is just one of the mechanisms designed to foster economic growth.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Likewise, inflation, interest rates, they are merely indicators to measure success.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Draghi: Indeed, the undertaking of structural reforms would complement the implementation of our expansionary monetary policy and would certainly have a multiplicative effect on growth and on the recovery.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: But then beyond a certain point, this is a completely national agenda and the ECB has a mandate to indicate which reforms are important because the lack of them could be an obstacle to achieving price stability.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: For example, in a situation where you have to raise inflation expectation towards the medium-term of 2% you want to have an accommodative monetary policy.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: At the same time you know that the more structural reforms are being undertaken, the more this monetary policy will be transmitted to the real economy.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: If banks are impaired, then the monetary policy, no matter how accommodative it could be, is not transmitted to the real economy and so, from this viewpoint, if the Capital Market Union can create a broader and better functioning capital markets, this is highly welcome.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: We welcome also your assessment replying to Mr Fernandez’ question, eligibility of the EIB [inaudible] bonds for the asset purchase programme.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Draghi: On the first point, well, first of all, we thought a lot about whether there is a relationship between the level of market interest rates and the incentives that governments have to undertake reforms.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: For example, do you really think that high level of interest rates in the markets would prove an incentive for a government to reform its educational system, or its judiciary, or its electoral system, or its constitution, or its labour market?

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: If we look at labour market reforms, they’ve taken place by and large when interest rates had already gone down very much.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: But, at the same time, there may be a relation between the budget size of a government and the interest rates.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: They have the expansionary effects of monetary policy propagated to the real economy through a variety of channels and that’s why we deemed that our expansionary monetary policy is needed to bring back inflation towards our objective of being close but below 2% over the medium-term.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: But, you have rejected, or would you reject launching any initiative of this kind that could improve the coherence of our monetary policy?

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Second question, risk of inflation in some member states.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Would that not affect inflation and monetary policy?

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: You hinted at two dangers here that our monetary policy might entail.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: First, let me state once again that we have a mandate and our mandate asks us to reach price stability as an objective, defined as I did before of having an inflation rate close but below 2% in the medium-term.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: We certainly monitor all these risks and the answer to these risks, however, should be found in the proper macro-prudential instruments, not in changing the monetary policy stance which is based on reaching our objective of price stability in fulfilling our mandate.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: We, all of us, by the way, it’s not only the ECB, the Federal Reserve, the Bank of England, Bank of Japan, run their monetary policy according to their mandates which are national mandates.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: So, even though we consult each other very frequently, we exchange views and information with all the partners in monetary policy making at global level, we have to take our decisions according to our national mandates which do not foresee other jurisdictions in the application of the mandate.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Interest rates, as you said, are extremely low in the EU.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Whether tone of the Federal Reserve seems to be becoming more and more moderate and possibly anticipating an increase in the interest rates in the coming months.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Draghi: On your first question, you know, the purchases are intended to be carried out until end September 2016 and will in any case be conducted until we see a sustained adjustment in the path of inflation which is consistent with our aim of achieving inflation rates below but close to 2% over the medium-term which means that we are not going to change our policy because of an observation at each point in time, or because of changes that are not sustained through time.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: So, there should be a sustained adjustment in the path of inflation which means that it will be the path of inflation, not its value at any point in time, and a consistent steady move of inflation, not a reversible blip in either direction that will speak for a change in our strategy.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: We are aware that very low interest rates carry this risk with themselves.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: But, as I said before, the response to these risks should come from the use of macro-prudential instruments, not from the change in our monetary policy stance which is geared to reaching our price stability objective.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: My second question is linked to the timing of quantitative easing and, of course, arguably quantitative easing is most effective when financial markets are in turmoil.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: There the question for you, do you feel that quantitative easing starts at the right moment in time?

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: My last very short question is did we understand you right in answering earlier the question on the end of quantitative easing?

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: Did we understand you right that if the path of inflation will not be in line with the objective of the ECB that you foresee the continuation of quantitative easing beyond September 2016, that you can imagine that?

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: The answer to your second question, in April 2014 last year in the course of a speech [ Monetary policy communication in turbulent times] I presented three contingencies that would make the ECB act.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: One was an unwanted tightening of money market.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: The second contingency was an impairment in the bank lending channel that would translate itself into an impairment of our transmission mechanism of the monetary policy.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: The third was a medium-term worsening of the inflation expectations horizon.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: We would act shortly thereafter to cope with the second contingency through the decision of the TLTROs which is targeting the banking system so that this could actually produce more lending to the real economy through the beginning of purchases of the ABS and the covered bond programme exactly with the same goal of trying to channel financing towards the real economy.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: But, size wise they were not enough so that by the beginning of August we see that medium-term inflation expectations start edging down and that’s when we had the Jackson Hole speech [ Unemployment in the euro area, 22 August 2014] and that’s when we started basically with the QE in mind.

titolo: Hearing at the European Parliament's Economic and Monetary Affairs Committee (introductory remarks and Q&A)
frase: We don’t see an especially illiquid situation for the government bonds and we are confident, as I said before, that in a smooth execution of our expanded asset purchase programme.

titolo: Introductory statement at the Italian Parliament
frase: Various factors are helping to boost confidence that the weak and uneven recovery experienced up to now will gain strength and stability and that inflation of a sustainable kind will return to the objective specified in the ECB’s mandate: a level below, but close to, 2%.

titolo: Introductory statement at the Italian Parliament
frase: There are three main factors that support these expectations of a pick-up: the positive effects of the fall in energy prices; our expansionary monetary policy, which has helped to reduce the fragmentation of the financial system and ensure that our low interest rates reach households and businesses; and the structural reforms carried out in various euro area countries, albeit at different speeds and intensity, which are now starting to have effects.

titolo: Introductory statement at the Italian Parliament
frase: It is the second and third points – monetary policy and structural policies – that I would like to focus on in my introductory remarks this afternoon.

titolo: Introductory statement at the Italian Parliament
frase: Monetary policy provides cyclical support to growth, which means that it helps the economy get back to its full potential.

titolo: Introductory statement at the Italian Parliament
frase: Similarly, monetary policy can achieve its price stability objective across the entire euro area, but only structural reforms can create real, lasting convergence in terms of productivity at national level.

titolo: Introductory statement at the Italian Parliament
frase: The role of monetary policy in the euro area You will remember that not so long ago, at the end of 2011 and 2012, we were facing a much less favourable environment than today.

titolo: Introductory statement at the Italian Parliament
frase: The transmission mechanism of the common monetary policy was no longer uniform in the individual countries.

titolo: Introductory statement at the Italian Parliament
frase: In this environment, the ability of the ECB to deliver price stability for the euro area as a whole was severely challenged.

titolo: Introductory statement at the Italian Parliament
frase: Monetary policy had to respond in a comprehensive way, commensurate with the multi-dimensional nature of the risk and simultaneously based on several channels running in parallel.

titolo: Introductory statement at the Italian Parliament
frase: First of all, for monetary policy to be effective again across the euro area we needed to remove those unwarranted fears about the ‘reversibility’ of the euro.

titolo: Introductory statement at the Italian Parliament
frase: With the Outright Monetary Transactions (OMTs), i.e.

titolo: Introductory statement at the Italian Parliament
frase: Together with our other non-standard measures, the OMTs have been decisive in reducing financial fragmentation.

titolo: Introductory statement at the Italian Parliament
frase: This in turn resulted in a more efficient transmission of monetary policy across the euro area.

titolo: Introductory statement at the Italian Parliament
frase: But further monetary policy action was called for.

titolo: Introductory statement at the Italian Parliament
frase: In June we adopted longer-term refinancing operations (TLTROs) to maintain bank lending to the economy.

titolo: Introductory statement at the Italian Parliament
frase: In September, as we had by then exhausted our margin to reduce interest rates, we moved to asset purchases as a means to ease financial conditions and thereby provide further support to the economy.

titolo: Introductory statement at the Italian Parliament
frase: This provides a key contribution to a full pick-up in economic activity and to keeping inflation from remaining too low for too long.

titolo: Introductory statement at the Italian Parliament
frase: First, the basis of the initial pick-up was still looking too weak to ensure that inflation would return to a level close to, but below, 2%.

titolo: Introductory statement at the Italian Parliament
frase: Second, the expansionary potential of the monetary policy interventions between June and October was still uncertain, because their effects depend on the decisions of the banks to make use of the Eurosystem loans, while the size of the private sector asset purchase programme may be fairly limited.

titolo: Introductory statement at the Italian Parliament
frase: The total take-up of loans under the two TLTROs came to €212.4 billion, in the lower range of possible forecasts.

titolo: Introductory statement at the Italian Parliament

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: The component of financial income that monetary policy affects most directly is net interest income, so it is useful to look at how the net interest income of different countries and sectors has been affected by falling interest rates during the crisis.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: What we find is that for large countries such as Spain and Germany the effect of low interest rates on the total economy has been positive – that is, they have received more in interest earnings than they have disbursed in interest payments.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: And second, the fact that the drop in interest rates on those liabilities has been significantly larger than on its assets, since Germany has acted as both a safe haven for investors during periods of financial stress, and as the premier safe-asset provider in the euro area in the context of the shrinking supply of AAA-rated government debt.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: But from what we can tell, there are no signs that low interest rates are shifting financial income away from stronger countries and towards weaker ones, as is often claimed.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: But this has been driven more by the earlier fall in interest rates in 2008 than the impact of our measures since mid-2014 – an issue I will return to later.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: Two waves have taken place so far – in 2010 and 2014 – which gives us the possibility to see how net financial income has shifted between different households as interest rates have fallen.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: Still, the distributional picture also has to take into account the second type of effects – wealth effects – which capture the impact of monetary policy on the value of financial assets.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: In this case the period we are most interested in is the one since mid-2014, as it is mostly asset purchases that are believed to create wealth inequality through asset price inflation.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: And it is important to remember that, to the degree that monetary policy has boosted asset prices, it has often been correcting previous falls in asset prices due to the crisis.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: In this sense, monetary policy has not been distorting the distribution of wealth, but rather restoring the distribution of the status quo ante.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: Bringing in the macroeconomic effects In any case, a balanced assessment of the distributional effects of monetary policy cannot focus only on its short-run financial effects.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: Even if low interest rates and high asset prices do worsen short-run inequality, they have positive distributional effects over the medium term.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: They lead to stronger aggregate demand, a faster fall in unemployment and medium-term price stability, all of which reduce inequality in the ways I described above.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: Alongside this are also the expansionary effects that monetary policy creates through its other channels: the exchange rate channel and intertemporal substitution.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: In particular, low interest rates encourage households to bring forward durable consumption, and firms’ investment, through credit.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: Pinning down the precise contribution of monetary policy to this is challenging, but we can see that since June 2014 our measures have triggered a downward convergence of bank lending rates and an upward trend in credit volumes, with borrowing costs in vulnerable countries now approaching those enjoyed by Germany and other stronger economies.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: Monetary policy has been a key driver.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: Yet monetary policy still appears to be having an endogenous impact on investment via aggregate demand.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: And even vis-à-vis the rest of the world, our monetary policy has helped insulate the euro area from the steep slowdown in world trade.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: The divergence between the monetary policy path of the euro area and that of other major economies was one factor supporting this.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: So we have every reason to believe that, with the impetus provided by our recent measures, monetary policy is working as expected: by boosting consumption and investment and creating jobs, which is always socially progressive.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: And importantly, we do not see any signs of another claim one sometimes hears: that low interest rates on savings are causing households to increase saving to maintain their lifecycle saving targets, thereby causing our policy to backfire.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: In other words, decisions by households are supporting the macroeconomic objectives of monetary policy, not countering it.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: This is also confirmed by survey evidence: the Bundesbank has found that just 1% of German households are saving more because of low interest rates.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: Raising the natural rate and returning to normal So if we net out the effects of the financial and macroeconomic channels, I find it hard to reach the conclusion that, over a longer time frame, the outcome of our policies has been – or will be – to redistribute wealth and income in an unfair or unequal way.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: What is more, as a recent study by the Bundesbank points out, those who claim that monetary policy worsens inequality typically do not consider the counterfactual.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: They take the distributional situation as given, but forget that monetary policy is acting precisely because the macroeconomic situation was at risk of changing.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: In fact, according to ECB simulations, euro area GDP would be cumulatively at least 1.5% lower between 2015 and 2018 without the expansionary policy measures we have adopted since mid-2014, with worse outcomes for inflation too.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: Yet all this does not mean that very low interest rates are costless.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: Indeed, we would certainly prefer not to have to keep interest rates at such low levels for an excessively long time, since the unwelcome side-effects may accumulate over time.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: But as very low interest rates persist, some of these offsetting factors, such as the capital gains will diminish, whereas the drawbacks will remain in place – for instance due to the downward stickiness of interest rates on retail deposits.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: Therefore we should seek to create the conditions for a return of interest rates to higher levels.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: The first are actions to bring output to potential without undue delay, so that inflation can return sustainably to our objective and policy interest rates can rise back to the natural rate.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: That is the best, indeed the only way for monetary policy to normalise.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: And this is why, looking ahead, we remain committed to preserving the very substantial degree of monetary accommodation which is necessary to secure a sustained convergence of inflation towards levels below, but close to, 2% over the medium term.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: But it is also clear that the more other macroeconomic stabilisation policies work alongside monetary policy, the faster the closure of the output gap will be.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: Still, returning to potential will not solve the fundamental problem we started with: the fact that the natural interest rate is itself very low.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: It is this that is ultimately driving interest rates down near zero.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: So the second type of actions we need, if we want interest rates at higher levels, are those that can raise the natural rate.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: In short, monetary policy is today protecting the interests of savers by ensuring a faster closing of the output gap and preserving the economic potential on which savers’ income depends.

titolo: Stability, equity and monetary policy
frase: But for real returns to rise further still, other policies need to buttress monetary policy by raising investment and productivity.

titolo: The euro area economy, monetary policy and structural reforms
frase: All these developments, of course, are gaining significant support from the effective pass-through of our accommodative monetary policy measures.

titolo: The euro area economy, monetary policy and structural reforms
frase: Taken together, our measures have led to a significant and broad-based easing in financing conditions through both price and quantity channels, which bolters consumption and investment expenditure.

titolo: The euro area economy, monetary policy and structural reforms

titolo: The euro area economy, monetary policy and structural reforms
frase: Favourable financing conditions, along with other factors such as employment gains and improvements in the demand outlook, are expected to further support private consumption and investment expenditure going forward.

titolo: The euro area economy, monetary policy and structural reforms
frase: Turning to price developments, headline inflation increased in September to 0.4% in year-on-year terms, owing mainly to a continued increase in annual energy inflation.

titolo: The euro area economy, monetary policy and structural reforms

frase: Underlying inflation in particular has yet to show clear signs of a more dynamic upward movement.

titolo: The euro area economy, monetary policy and structural reforms
frase: The annual rate of HICP inflation excluding food and energy has continued to hover around 1% as domestic cost pressures remain fundamentally weak.

titolo: The euro area economy, monetary policy and structural reforms
frase: Yet, as the effect of past oil price declines fades, annual HICP inflation is expected to pick up from 0.2% this year to 1.2% in 2017.

titolo: The euro area economy, monetary policy and structural reforms
frase: Moreover, we expect that as the recovery continues and economic slack falls, inflation will gradually accelerate further to 1.6% in 2018.

titolo: The euro area economy, monetary policy and structural reforms
frase: Moreover, our baseline scenario for growth and inflation in the euro area remains crucially dependent on the current supportive financing conditions staying in place.

titolo: The euro area economy, monetary policy and structural reforms
frase: Therefore, we will ensure that monetary policy continues to play its role in facilitating the cyclical recovery.

titolo: The euro area economy, monetary policy and structural reforms
frase: By ensuring accommodative financing conditions that buoy demand, monetary policy is helping to raise output back to its potential level.

titolo: The euro area economy, monetary policy and structural reforms
frase: As reiterated after last week’s Governing Council meeting, we remain committed to preserving the very substantial amount of monetary accommodation which is necessary to secure a sustained convergence of inflation towards levels below, but close to, 2% over the medium term.

titolo: The euro area economy, monetary policy and structural reforms
frase: However, such reforms are outside of the scope of monetary policy and fall under the remit of other national and European policymakers.

titolo: The euro area economy, monetary policy and structural reforms
frase: As the benefits of structural reforms can take time to materialise, they must be implemented without undue delay and are needed in order to reap the full benefits from our monetary policy measures.

titolo: The euro area economy, monetary policy and structural reforms
frase: The highly accommodative stance of monetary policy creates ideal conditions for the implementation of structural policies, as it can help to cushion the potential short-term adjustment costs of such policies by supporting current demand conditions.

titolo: The euro area economy, monetary policy and structural reforms
frase: The support to demand from monetary policy must be complemented with supply policies that bolster the potential growth, productivity and flexibility of the euro area economy.

titolo: Low interest rate environment – an economic, legal and social analysis
frase: In his main work “Geldzins und Güterpreise” (1898), Knut Wicksell investigated the influence of monetary policy on investment and savings behaviour, as well as on the economy.

titolo: Low interest rate environment – an economic, legal and social analysis
frase: He stated that if the key interest rate is reduced to below the natural interest rate, savings are lower and consumption is higher.

titolo: Low interest rate environment – an economic, legal and social analysis
frase: The natural rate is “the loan interest rate at which this reacts in an entirely neutral way to goods prices.”

titolo: Low interest rate environment – an economic, legal and social analysis
frase: Interest rate cuts thus lead to loan creation, investment and greater consumption.

titolo: Low interest rate environment – an economic, legal and social analysis
frase: Conversely, higher interest rates dampen demand and price increases.

titolo: Low interest rate environment – an economic, legal and social analysis
frase: In short: if the market rate is lower than the natural rate, inflation will tend to occur, and when the opposite is true, then disinflation or even deflation are likely to result.

titolo: Low interest rate environment – an economic, legal and social analysis
frase: If then in such an environment further economic shocks occur on the demand side, the central bank has to resort rather to unconventional measures, as it can only lower the policy rate to a limited extent.

titolo: Low interest rate environment – an economic, legal and social analysis

titolo: Low interest rate environment – an economic, legal and social analysis

titolo: Low interest rate environment – an economic, legal and social analysis

titolo: Low interest rate environment – an economic, legal and social analysis
